A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Seq-VCR work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 Small and minGPT experiments on multiplication, Arithmetic Expressions, and LIS, including representation analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results on regularization variants, larger models, CodeXGLUE, C4, and GSM8K.

M1.justification: The principal loss, projection, and pause-token procedure are retained. Appendices F and H additionally evaluate a variant computing covariance jointly across batch and sequence dimensions rather than only across the batch, a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: Appendices K–M add CodeXGLUE text-to-code, C4 language-model pretraining, and an enhanced GSM8K math-word-problem dataset. These substantially broaden the original multiplication, Arithmetic Expressions, and LIS coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 8 adds CoT to the depth comparisons for Arithmetic Expressions and LIS, which previously compared only Vanilla, Pause, and Seq-VCR. Table 1 retains the same comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-2 multiplication training from scratch, Llama3.2-1B fine-tuning with rank-64 LoRA, diagnostics across 1B/3B/8B models, normalized throughput, and C4 validation perplexity. Original training schedules remain unchanged. Section 3.5's new claim of two pause tokens in all experiments conflicts with Section 4.6's retained four- and seven-token settings.

E4.justification: v2 expands Figure 10's pause-token analysis across arithmetic difficulties and adds covariance-axis, regularized-layer, pretraining-versus-scratch, model-scale, and speed–accuracy analyses in Appendices E–J. Figure 9's depth-versus-difficulty analysis already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions report three seed runs for Figures 7–9 and display error bars there. v2 adds no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1's headline 0.992/0.995 Seq-VCR+Pause accuracies remain unchanged. New results include 0.974 Llama accuracy in Table 8 and GSM8K accuracies of 0.202 for Seq-VCR+Pause, 0.191 for Vanilla, and 0.437 for CoT in Table 9. v2 also adds throughput and ablation results, expands Figure 10, and reports similar C4 perplexity despite increased representation entropy.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds an asymptotic computational-cost comparison, O(bd^2) versus O(bnd^2), absent from v1. The entropy and loss formulations remain unchanged; new Equation 4 explicitly spells out the existing covariance calculation rather than introducing a new theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: intermediate representation collapse limits reasoning, and Seq-VCR with pause tokens improves performance without explicit CoT supervision. The headline 99.5% multiplication claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving pause-token distractions when model capacity is sufficient, shared pause embeddings, layer-specific failures, and greater sensitivity when training from scratch. It also extends applicability interpretations to larger models and other domains. Appendix E introduces a stronger, unqualified claim that Seq-VCR always scales better than CoT regardless of model size.

D1.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendix A newly disclose eta=0.001, task-specific regularizer coefficients, manual hyperparameter selection, projector placement and training, and the pause-token input format. Added experiments specify LoRA rank and C4 layer-specific coefficients. These substantially improve implementation documentation, although some new benchmark protocols remain sparse; the original code-access link is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Skean et al. (2024), removes Park et al. (2024) and Renyi (1961), and changes the stated justification for the linear kernel. Section 3.4 more explicitly positions Seq-VCR as directly repurposing VICReg/VCReg formulations, while the broader literature review remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are retained. v2 rewrites and expands the entropy, regularization, and pause-token explanations, adds a paper roadmap, corrects wording and publication headers, and organizes the earlier appendix material into descriptive sections A–D before the new studies.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–9 and Figures 11–15, adds CoT bars and legends to Figure 8, and substantially redraws Figure 10 with complexity-specific series. Existing figures and tables are also resized or relocated, producing a substantial expansion of the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's validation centered on small models and synthetic tasks and omitted essential regularizer settings. v2 substantially strengthens the paper through controlled design and initialization studies, larger-model and broader-domain tests, efficiency measurements, and implementation disclosures. Similar C4 perplexity and modest GSM8K gains also make the method's practical scope easier to assess. Conflicting pause-token statements, incomplete new protocols, and the overbroad scalability claim limit confidence, but do not outweigh these substantial gains in validation and reproducibility information.
